### 2026-10-05 — **5th October:**

**7h**

**5th October:**

**Morning:** I got off to work on my idea for week 1, which is a macro pad... and I researched online for the best microcontrollers for my macropad, and I got to know that XIAO RP2350 is the best board for my case. Then I looked into a GitHub repo of a friend of mine to know what exactly I am dealing with.

![rp2350](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/d7w40VcNe9cOircr9SSeVPctkrTODbXr/5e68e5775d87c97b5990f0322cf03bcd6ca46b0642a7bbce6a6633700b053f5d.jpeg)

And also got to know what exactly hot-swappable keys are because I really don't know what those were.

![what exactly are hot swappable keys](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/d7w40VcNe9cOircr9SSeVPctkrTODbXr/0361f5c1f6e05b3001f49e969b0f1618fa39753796e461db1c6fcb381542d95a.jpeg)

Later, I made my GitHub repo and named it Tecjay Macropad, as Tecjay sounds cool, and it was named after my favourite character of fiction, Tech Jacket.

![github](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/d7w40VcNe9cOircr9SSeVPctkrTODbXr/2d0c96c90339286679704feb8f080995b693d9d06e21926702f7802a779488cd.jpeg)
Then I started off on KiCad and installed the required symbol folders and the required footprint libraries for the project. I then started the schematics of the project.

**Afternoon:** So, I made the plan that I am going to have a rows and column layout as I don't have enough pins on the board and got to work on schematics. The image below is the image showing me completing column 1 of the layout.

![added column1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/d7w40VcNe9cOircr9SSeVPctkrTODbXr/1ec27b8bc86fa65a0939664612588a44a41a1ae1a3003d28508228ee753e92e5.jpeg)

I quickly started column 2 and finished it in like 10 minutes.

![added column2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/d7w40VcNe9cOircr9SSeVPctkrTODbXr/bb1ce637859a1f1ff0ba3fa83337382c22a7e69306df689514b3ba181dad3388.jpeg)

And finished column 3 in 10 minutes, but my schematics got very messy in between, so I had to change the layout.

![added column3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/d7w40VcNe9cOircr9SSeVPctkrTODbXr/b749388fef8205f64eb659e28c17228522e636f0b99f88651cf7e9e7574adf33.jpeg)
Then I got to work on the RGB LEDs, but I placed all of the 9 LEDs and was faced with an issue when I tried to run the Electrical Rules Checker and ran into errors. I asked my friends in the Half Life Slack to know what the issue was. I was not placing the power flags and had not labelled the wires, so I got back and fixed the issue and wired all of the 9 LEDs together.

![added leds](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/d7w40VcNe9cOircr9SSeVPctkrTODbXr/076228bae9d5af2f66c793b8331545eb269f5367a6ded946b76da791c23661d8.jpeg)

Then my friends from Slack suggested that I place a resistor and a capacitor for the LEDs for the safety of the LEDs. I then got to know that the LEDs I am using are not meant for 3.3V, so I changed the footprints and started using another set of LEDs. I then placed the OLED screen and the potentiometer, which happened to be the easiest thing out of all the components to place.

![final end of the day](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/d7w40VcNe9cOircr9SSeVPctkrTODbXr/619011ce3dfb498d9648b1e88eb916c8a1b8acf0866b1b5e18b45fb30874cb25.jpeg)
